items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: My brother. Violin. Violin was always the leader... and then we'd play

ctx.x: My brother. Violin. Violin was always the leader, if you had one. Always. He was the one who would knock off the tunes, and then we'd play the (?).
In those days what kind of time signatures did you play in?

Around Algiers and all them other little old towns, in Reserve or... Any little town. Because we played East St. Louis, and I would get tired of staying on that bus, and we'd come into St. Louis. That's how I happened to meet Charlie Creath and Zutty and them guys around there, in 1925.
We're going to get to that a little bit later. Let me just pursue this a bit further with Doc Moon.
